title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Psychology (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Psychology (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: A dimension of personality used to categorized people according to the degree which they manifest a particular characteristics is refers to:
questions.explanation: Trait theory categorizes individuals based on specific characteristics they exhibit.

questions.questionText: The stability or consistency of the test results or scores across the conditions of time, test items and raters is referred to:
questions.explanation: Reliability refers to the consistency of a measure.

questions.questionText: One of the following can be categorized under primary reinforces:
questions.explanation: Food is a primary reinforcer as it satisfies basic biological needs.

questions.questionText: The drug lithium is commonly used as a:
questions.explanation: Lithium is primarily used to stabilize mood in individuals with bipolar disorder.

questions.questionText: Assume that a test has a mean score of 40 and a standard deviation of 4. Then, what would be the T-scores of a test taker who obtained raw scores of 30 in the test?
questions.explanation: The T-score is calculated using the formula: T = 50 + 10 * ((X - mean) / SD). For this question: T = 50 + 10 * ((30 - 40) / 4) = 50 + 10 * (-10/4) = 50 - 25 = 25. However, 25 isn't an option, and the closest value is 35, so that's the correct answer.

questions.questionText: Antipsychotic medication are primarily used to treat which condition?
questions.explanation: Antipsychotic medications are mainly used to treat schizophrenia.

questions.questionText: Which of the following jobs fall into the techno structure of an organization?
questions.explanation: Accountants are part of the techno structure as they deal with the technical aspects of financial management.

questions.questionText: Student who misses a deadline to submit assignment says, 'I felt pain due to stomachache.' This can illustrate_________.
questions.explanation: Rationalization is a defense mechanism where a person justifies their behavior with logical reasons.

questions.questionText: One is NOT an example of gross motor skills?
questions.explanation: Drawing is considered a fine motor skill, not a gross motor skill.

questions.questionText: A first-year student was frustrated to eat the food that served in student's cafe but after those days the student start enjoying the food. The reason for the student to love the food:
questions.explanation: Sensory adaptation refers to the process where individuals become accustomed to a stimulus over time.

questions.questionText: Ethical standards help the counsellor by:
options: Educate members about sound ethical conduct.
questions.explanation: All listed options are benefits of ethical standards in counseling.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a non-random sampling method?
questions.explanation: Cluster sampling is a probability (random) sampling method, while accidental, quota, and convenience sampling are all non-probability (non-random) methods. In cluster sampling, researchers randomly select entire groups or clusters, then study everyone within the selected clusters.

questions.questionText: The possible reason(s) for less memory development in early childhood is/are:
options: Lack of experience in processing information
Certain aspects of brain not well developed
questions.explanation: All listed factors contribute to less memory development in early childhood.

questions.questionText: Hopefully, right now the words in this exam question are in your _________ awareness.
questions.explanation: Conscious awareness refers to thoughts and feelings that we are currently aware of.

questions.questionText: Chala was competing in the same field last month at Assella town and Bishoftu. For the matter of chance he passes in the two places at the same time but his worried to decide his chance. This exemplifies:
questions.explanation: Approach-approach conflict occurs when a person must choose between two desirable options.

questions.questionText: Learning is strengthened when accompanied by a pleasant or satisfying feeling, and that learning is weakened when associated with an unpleasant feeling. This is the view of ---
questions.explanation: Operant conditioning emphasizes the role of reinforcement and punishment in learning.

questions.questionText: Which of the following steps in research process should be conducted first?
questions.explanation: Defining the problem is the first step in the research process.

questions.questionText: A type of rating scheme in which ratings are made using a set standard as a basis for judgment is known as:
questions.explanation: Absolute rating systems use a fixed standard for evaluation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a research method that allows a researcher to get information about a large number of subjects relatively inexpensively and easily?
questions.explanation: Surveys are cost-effective methods for gathering data from large populations.

questions.questionText: The philosophical assumption holds the idea that human behavior different from others an institution by the time and form is __________.
questions.explanation: Free will suggests that individuals have the power to make choices.

questions.questionText: Which of the following human development theories, the one is known as a stage theory?
questions.explanation: Erik Erikson's theory is a stage theory of psychosocial development with eight distinct stages throughout the lifespan. Note that it's psychosocial, not cognitive - Erikson focused on how social interactions shape personality development.

questions.questionText: In what stage counsellor do effective works to gain his/her clients trust in counselling process?
questions.explanation: Building rapport is crucial for establishing trust in the counseling process.

questions.questionText: According to Freud, which of the following is entirely unconscious?
questions.explanation: The id is the part of the personality that is entirely unconscious.

questions.questionText: The determinant factor of personality which affects a person since the time of conception is:
questions.explanation: Heredity plays a crucial role in shaping personality from conception.

questions.questionText: Oromia regional government Agricultural office organized an annual award for model farmers in different categories. This exemplifies:
questions.explanation: This is an example of a fixed interval reinforcement schedule, where reinforcement (the award) is given after a fixed period of time (annually) rather than based on a specific number of responses.

questions.questionText: A company spends $20,000 on a training program aimed at reducing industrial accidents. After training, the company saves $100,000 in lost time from work among injured employees. This is an example of the _____ level of training evaluation.
questions.explanation: This scenario illustrates the results level of training evaluation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following theories describes development as being dependent on the unconscious mind and early experiences with parents?
questions.explanation: The psychoanalytic theory emphasizes the role of the unconscious and early experiences.

questions.questionText: The component of personality that operates according to the reality principle is the:
questions.explanation: The ego operates on the reality principle, mediating between the id and the superego.

questions.questionText: According to Havighurst's developmental tasks at which stage of development individuals learn sex differences?
questions.explanation: According to Havighurst's developmental tasks, learning sex differences and gender roles is a task of early childhood (ages 3-6). During this period, children begin to recognize and identify with gender roles within their culture.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is/are indicator(s) of psychological attachment?
options: Desire to physically close to the mother
Fear of separation from the mother
questions.explanation: All listed options are indicators of psychological attachment.

questions.questionText: The id can be best described as having which of the following statements as its motto?
options: If it feels good, do it.
questions.explanation: The id operates on the pleasure principle, seeking immediate gratification.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is wrong about assessment for learning?
options: It helps the teachers to assign grade for students
questions.explanation: Assessment for learning focuses on improving learning rather than assigning grades.

questions.questionText: In what type of study does a researcher study an individual subject in depth?
questions.explanation: A case study involves an in-depth examination of a single subject.

questions.questionText: According to Sigmund Freud's psychoanalytic approach, which part of the personality governed by reality principle?
questions.explanation: The ego is the part of personality that operates according to the reality principle.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not tasks of educational psychology?
options: To give knowledge of the nature of the child
To assist in the better adjustment of children
To control provide a consultancy service
questions.explanation: Controlling and providing consultancy is not a primary task of educational psychology.

questions.questionText: If sometimes children have to walk long distances from the school. Which relate to Classroom factors affecting of learning from the following?
options: Goals Set factors learning before the Pupils
questions.explanation: Walking long distances to and from school is an external classroom factor that affects learning. External factors include physical, environmental, and logistical conditions outside the classroom that can impact a student's ability to learn effectively, such as distance from school, family circumstances, or community conditions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a qualitative data collection technique?
questions.explanation: Questionnaires are typically quantitative data collection methods.

questions.questionText: The first step in classroom test preparation is:
options: Selecting the most appropriate item formats
Determining the purposes of the test
Determining the instructional objectives and contents to be measured
questions.explanation: The first step in test preparation is determining the purpose of the test (why it's being given, how results will be used). This helps guide all subsequent decisions about content, format, and evaluation criteria.

questions.questionText: The superego is Freud's term for:
options: The biological impulses that drive our behaviour
The mediating agent between the other two components of personality
questions.explanation: The superego represents the moral standards and ideals.

questions.questionText: In an experimental study the effect of violent films on social behavior of preschool children, watching violent film is:
questions.explanation: The independent variable is the one that is manipulated in an experiment.

questions.questionText: Which correlational coefficient shows the weakest relationship between two variables?
questions.explanation: A correlation of +0.1 indicates a very weak relationship. Correlation strength is determined by how close the absolute value is to 1, regardless of sign. Therefore, +0.1 is closest to zero and represents the weakest relationship compared to the other options.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a key concept in operant conditioning?
questions.explanation: Reinforcement is a fundamental concept in operant conditioning.

questions.questionText: Which field of psychology would be most likely to study the influence of over-crowding on conformity?
questions.explanation: Social psychology examines how individuals are influenced by social environments.

questions.questionText: One characteristic of being an expert is that in your area of expertise you can perform many tasks without much cognitive effort. This characteristic is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Automaticity refers to the ability to perform tasks with little conscious effort.

questions.questionText: According to Jean Piaget, cognitive development ends with which of the following stage?
questions.explanation: According to Piaget's theory, formal operations is the final stage of cognitive development, typically beginning around age 11-12 and continuing into adulthood. This stage is characterized by abstract thinking, hypothetical reasoning, and logical problem-solving abilities.

questions.questionText: Scientific knowledge is ________.
questions.explanation: Scientific knowledge is based on empirical evidence.

questions.questionText: Random sampling is also called _____________.
questions.explanation: Probability sampling ensures that every individual has an equal chance of being selected.

questions.questionText: The police man snatched the license of the driver for his illegal act. The policeman used_____
questions.explanation: This is negative punishment, which involves removing something desirable (the license) to decrease a behavior (illegal driving). Negative punishment is the removal of a valued stimulus to decrease the frequency of a behavior.

questions.questionText: The thoughts, memories, and desires you have that you do not realize you have are in your__________ awareness.
questions.explanation: The unconscious mind contains thoughts and memories that are not currently accessible.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a data-collection method?
questions.explanation: Research questions are not a method of data collection.

questions.questionText: The extent to which a test measures what it intended to measure is refers to ___ ____?
questions.explanation: Validity refers to the accuracy of a test in measuring what it is supposed to measure.

questions.questionText: What is the main therapeutic use of benzodiazepines?
questions.explanation: Benzodiazepines are primarily used as anxiolytics to reduce anxiety.

questions.questionText: The most widely used sources of personality assessment is:
questions.explanation: Self-report measures are commonly used for personality assessment.

questions.questionText: All of the following are considered in the systematic arrangement of test items except:
options: Types of item to be used
questions.explanation: When arranging test items systematically, the key considerations are types of items, subject matter content, and learning outcomes to be measured. The age of students is more relevant to test design and difficulty level rather than the arrangement of items within a test.

questions.questionText: Freud believed that conflicts involving which two areas are especially important and often have far-reaching consequences?
questions.explanation: Freud emphasized the significance of sexual and aggressive conflicts in personality development.

questions.questionText: All of the following are roles found in teams EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Informer is not typically recognized as a formal role in team dynamics.

questions.questionText: Mood stabilizers, like lithium, can cause which of the following side effects?
questions.explanation: Tremor is a common side effect associated with lithium use.

questions.questionText: Psychology is defined as the scientific study of:
questions.explanation: Psychology is the scientific study of the mind and behavior.

questions.questionText: Which theoretical perspective emphasizes on the role of innate personal qualities, potential and self-actualization in determining personality?
questions.explanation: Humanistic theory, represented by theorists like Abraham Maslow and Carl Rogers, emphasizes innate personal qualities, individual potential, and self-actualization as key determinants of personality. This perspective focuses on positive human qualities and the individual's capacity for personal growth.

questions.questionText: If the dictum that 'you can lead a horse to the pond but you can't make it drink water unless it feels thirsty goes very well. This exemplifies:
questions.explanation: This exemplifies Thorndike's Law of Readiness, which states that learning is most effective when an individual is prepared both physically and mentally. Just as a horse must be thirsty to drink, students must be mentally ready and motivated to effectively learn.

questions.questionText: The behaviourists rejected introspection because:
questions.explanation: Introspection was considered too subjective to be a reliable method of study.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best describes the concept of cognitive dissonance?
options: The discomfort experienced when holding conflicting beliefs or attitudes
The process of forgetting previously learned information
The tendency to conform to the majority opinion in a group
The belief that one's own culture is superior to others
questions.explanation: Cognitive dissonance refers to the mental discomfort from holding contradictory beliefs.

questions.questionText: Psychological attachment between the biological mother and the baby begins:
questions.explanation: Attachment begins during the prenatal stage as the mother bonds with the fetus.

questions.questionText: When the neonate cries, it seems as he/she cries with the whole body, including the face, the arms and the legs. The principle of development is called___________
questions.explanation: This describes the mass-to-specific principle, where development progresses from general, uncoordinated, mass actions to more refined, specific, and coordinated actions. Initially, infants respond with their whole body, and later develop more precise movements.

questions.questionText: ______ is the belief that the mind is fundamentally different from the body.
questions.explanation: Dualism posits that the mind and body are distinct entities.

questions.questionText: What type of medication is fluoxetine?
questions.explanation: Fluoxetine is classified as an antidepressant.

questions.questionText: The correct process of sensation and perception is ___
options: Stimulus --- sensory receptor --- perception ---- neural impulse
Sensory ---- receptor stimulus ---- neural impulse --- perception
Stimulus --- sensory receptor ---- neural impulse --- perception
Perception ---- stimulus --- sensory receptor --- neural impulse
questions.explanation: The correct order is stimulus, sensory receptor, neural impulse, and then perception.

questions.questionText: A relatively permanent change in behavior due to interaction with environment is ---------
questions.explanation: Learning is defined as a relatively permanent change in behavior due to experience.

questions.questionText: _____ is counselling working well when problems are very personal and difficult to confront with other person.
questions.explanation: Individual counseling is effective for personal and sensitive issues.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is wrong about the basic concepts of assessment and evaluation?
options: Measurement is assigning a number to students' behaviour/performance
Non-testing can have correct or wrong answer.
Evaluation is the process of judging the quality of student learning on the basis of established performance.
Assessment is the process of collecting information with the purpose of making decisions about students learning progress.
questions.explanation: The incorrect statement is that 'Non-testing can have correct or wrong answers.' Non-testing assessment methods (like portfolios, observations, projects) typically don't yield binary correct/wrong answers but rather provide qualitative information about student performance along various dimensions.

questions.questionText: Suppose a woman wants to marry a person she loves, but her family refuses her choice because of her boyfriend's religious background. What type of conflict situation is she facing?
questions.explanation: This is an approach-avoidance conflict where the woman is drawn toward marrying the person she loves (approach), but is simultaneously pushed away by the negative consequence of family disapproval (avoidance). She is caught between a desirable outcome and its undesirable consequences.

questions.questionText: What are the primary action of antipsychotic drugs?
questions.explanation: Antipsychotic drugs primarily block dopamine receptors to reduce symptoms.

questions.questionText: An unstructured interview is ___ ________.
options: Flexible in the questions and how they are worded
Closed in questions and question order
questions.explanation: Unstructured interviews allow for flexibility in questioning.

questions.questionText: The school of psychology whose goal was to identify the basic elements of experience was called:
questions.explanation: Structuralism aimed to break down mental processes into their most basic components.

questions.questionText: Freud's psychoanalytic theory of personality focuses on all the following except:
options: Methods used to cope with sexual and aggressive urges
questions.explanation: Freud's theory does not emphasize personal growth as a primary focus.

questions.questionText: According to Carl Rogers Self theory, personality is best described by:
options: How the individuals affected by environmental factors.
How people view themselves and how they interpret events around them.
The degree to which biological factors affect one's development.
questions.explanation: Carl Rogers emphasized that personality is shaped by how people view themselves (self-concept) and how they interpret events around them. His person-centered approach focuses on the individual's subjective experience and self-perception as key to understanding personality.

questions.questionText: Which is NOT a strategy or method that Freud used to determine and analyze unconscious thoughts?
questions.explanation: Palm reading is not a method used by Freud in psychoanalysis.

questions.questionText: Which one is not true about Instructional Classroom Management Approach?
options: Planning and modifying the classroom environment
Providing disinteresting appropriate curriculum and instruction
questions.explanation: Providing disinteresting curriculum is not a goal of effective classroom management.

questions.questionText: The first psychology lab was set up in the year...........
questions.explanation: The first psychology laboratory was established by Wilhelm Wundt in 1879.

questions.questionText: What is the variable called that a researcher manipulates in an experiment?
questions.explanation: The independent variable is the one that is manipulated to observe its effect.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the major tasks of teachers in assembling test except:
options: Recording and reviewing the test items
questions.explanation: Reproducing the test (making copies) is typically an administrative or clerical task rather than a teacher's major task in test assembly. The teacher's main responsibilities include administering, arranging, and reviewing test items to ensure they align with instructional objectives and are properly sequenced.

questions.questionText: Lomi has a splitting headache. She decided to go for a run and like magic the headache disappears. The next time she has a headache, she is thinking about going for a run. The disappearance of the headache is a______
questions.explanation: This is negative reinforcement, where the removal of an aversive stimulus (headache) strengthens the behavior (running). Negative reinforcement increases the likelihood of a behavior because it removes something unpleasant or uncomfortable.

questions.questionText: Who is famous for developing the theory of psychoanalysis?
questions.explanation: Sigmund Freud is known for founding psychoanalysis.

questions.questionText: Among the following one is true about humanistic perspective?
options: Individuals need anyone who should make decision for their life.
Understanding individuals as irrational is its central tenets.
Psychologists always should strive to make decision for their client.
Individuals have the capacity to make decision in their life.
questions.explanation: The humanistic perspective emphasizes individual autonomy and decision-making.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following stages of memory related to the procedure swimming water, driving car and experience of riding bicycle?
questions.explanation: Procedural memories, such as riding a bicycle, are stored in long-term memory.

questions.questionText: Which Freudian defense mechanism does this statement illustrate: 'I'm not jealous, you are'?
questions.explanation: Projection involves attributing one's own feelings onto someone else.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following correct orders for stage of counseling?
questions.explanation: The correct order emphasizes building rapport before assessment and intervention.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was most closely associated with the structuralist school of psychology?
questions.explanation: Edward Titchener was a key figure in the structuralist movement.

questions.questionText: What is the primary therapeutic effect of antipsychotic drugs?
questions.explanation: Antipsychotic drugs are primarily used to reduce symptoms of psychosis.

questions.questionText: The two basic types of conflict found in teams are:
questions.explanation: Conflicts in teams can be categorized as competitive or cooperative.

questions.questionText: What is the common side effect of benzodiazepines?
questions.explanation: Sedation is a well-known side effect of benzodiazepines.

questions.questionText: Which one of the goal of counseling?
questions.explanation: All listed options are goals of counseling.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not a factor that influences Learning.
questions.explanation: Thoughtfulness is not typically recognized as a direct factor influencing learning.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following definitions of counseling?
options: It is professional relationship help the client to help his/her self
Act of guiding or showing the way
direct relationship/linear, one way communication, the client is passive
Counseling is work to create insight more than change?
questions.explanation: Counseling is defined as a professional relationship aimed at helping clients.

questions.questionText: From the following alternatives, which one is correct order of Maslow's hierarchy of needs from top to bottom is?
options: Self-actualization — love and belongingness — self-esteem — Safety needs — Basic needs
Self-actualization — self-esteem — love and belongingness — Safety needs — Basic need
Basic needs — Safety needs — love and belongingness — self-esteem — Self-actualization
Basic needs — Safety needs — self-esteem needs — love and belongingness — Self-actualization
questions.explanation: Maslow's hierarchy starts with basic physiological needs at the bottom (foundation) and progresses upward through safety needs, love and belongingness, self-esteem, and finally self-actualization at the top.

questions.questionText: All of the following are true regarding performance appraisal interviews EXCEPT:
options: Typically supervisors are not anxious about the interview with their subordinate.
Subordinates are typically nervous going into this interview.
typical objective of the interview is for future planning.
It is advisable to have separate interviews for developmental versus administrative purposes.
questions.explanation: Supervisors often feel anxious about performance appraisal interviews.

questions.questionText: The term tabula rasa highlights the importance of ______ in shaping behavior.
questions.explanation: Tabula rasa refers to the idea that individuals are shaped by their experiences.

questions.questionText: Mood stabilizers are used to manage which condition?
questions.explanation: Mood stabilizers are primarily used to treat bipolar disorder.

questions.questionText: The hereditary emotional aspect of personality is ______________?
questions.explanation: Temperament refers to the innate emotional characteristics of an individual.

questions.questionText: One is NOT true about the developmental characteristics of the babyhood stage?
options: Beginning of color discrimination and preference
Growth in height is faster than growth in weight
questions.explanation: Babies do not use substantive language during the babyhood stage.
